conceptZh: 玩具警犬追查失蹤餅乾，先聞聞「犬」字右上方的一點，最後發現餅乾竟然黏在豬探長的帽頂！
object: A toy police dog, a friendly cartoon pig detective, and a tiny biscuit stuck to the detective’s hat.
morph: The complete glyph remains intact throughout. The dog briefly investigates its upper-right dot before following the biscuit scent to the detective’s hat.
creativeAngle: 把右上角的一點變成查案時的可疑線索；警犬的伸縮鼻子找到帽頂餅乾，豬探長卻還在用放大鏡找地板，形成短而清楚的反差笑點。
promptEn:
Create an exactly 8-second stylized 3D toy animation in a fixed, front-facing composition. Center one correctly formed Traditional Chinese glyph 犬, rendered in saturated cobalt blue against a softly lit pale cream background. Use an authentic Traditional Chinese typeface with four clearly separated, correctly placed strokes, especially the distinct upper-right dot. The glyph fills approximately 70% of frame height, with generous margins, and stays centered, fully visible and uncropped throughout. A small friendly cartoon pig detective with a plain toy hat and magnifying glass occupies the left margin; a small mechanical toy police dog with rounded paws and an unmarked blue harness occupies the right margin. Keep their actions outside the strokes. A tiny golden biscuit is stuck to the top of the detective’s hat.
From 0.0–1.4 seconds, the detective earnestly inspects the floor through the magnifying glass while the dog raises its nose toward the glyph’s upper-right dot. From 1.4–2.3 seconds, the dog gives the dot one investigative sniff, pauses, then swivels toward the hat as its ears perk up. From 2.3–3.7 seconds, its clearly mechanical accordion nose extends comically across the open space above the glyph and gently taps the biscuit. The detective keeps searching the floor for one extra beat, then looks upward, cross-eyed at the biscuit on its own hat. The dog retracts its nose with the biscuit balanced on its tip. From 3.7–4.7 seconds, the delighted dog and sheepishly smiling detective roll out through the side edges, taking every prop with them. From 4.7–8.0 seconds, hold only the complete, unobstructed glyph 犬 perfectly still for 3.3 full seconds. Keep lighting bright and soft, colors cheerful without neon, and the action warm and harmless.
Audio: a warm, friendly off-screen voice speaks clear Taiwanese Mandarin. The ONLY spoken line is exactly "犬、犬、警犬". Say the first 犬 around 0.5 seconds, the second 犬 around 1.7 seconds, and 警犬 naturally around 5.3–6.4 seconds during the finished glyph hold. Pronunciation lock: 犬 = ㄑㄩㄢˇ, quǎn; 警犬 = jǐng quǎn. Both isolated readings and 犬 within 警犬 use the same quǎn reading. Bopomofo and pinyin are silent pronunciation directions, never spoken or displayed. Stop after 警犬. Allow only soft sniffing and a quiet mechanical nose sound beneath the voice; no music or additional dialogue. The single glyph 犬 is the only on-screen text: no vocabulary text, subtitles, written names, logos, watermark, clutter, or flashing effects.
direction:

The dog finds a missing biscuit stuck to the detective’s hat. Use clearly stylized toys or cartoon animals; costume characters must be obviously toy/robot figures. Keep the character itself and its meaning central; the prop gag is brief and the final glyph remains correct, unobstructed, large and still for at least 3 seconds. No logos or written character names on screen.
PRONUNCIATION LOCK: target 犬, Bopomofo ㄑㄩㄢˇ, Mandarin pinyin quǎn. The ONLY spoken line must be exactly "犬、犬、警犬". Example word is fixed as 警犬, pronounced jǐng quǎn. Do not substitute a word. Both isolated readings and the target syllable inside the word must have exactly the same reading. Include this exact spoken line and these pronunciation guides explicitly in promptEn, stating that Bopomofo/pinyin are silent pronunciation directions, never spoken or displayed. Use clear Taiwanese Mandarin, no extra dialogue, no character catchphrases. Avoid other polyphonic examples or reading alternatives anywhere in the narration instructions. Themes affect the visual gag only, never the spoken vocabulary.

conceptZh: 發條小狗樂團想演奏威風的開場，喇叭卻吹出汪汪聲，引發鈸片撞擊、大鼓翻倒，最後整團搖尾巴謝幕。
object: An original wind-up dog trio with a trumpet, cymbals and a bass drum, surrounding a solid blue 犬.
morph: The complete glyph remains unchanged; the dogs demonstrate its meaning through a barking trumpet and an unmistakably canine tail-wagging finale.
creativeAngle: 改用一本正經卻演奏失敗的發條狗樂團：喇叭汪一聲，鈸手嚇得合鈸，大鼓再緩緩翻倒。以連鎖失誤呈現「狗」的意思，完整字形始終固定，尤其保留右上獨立的一點，避免看成「大」。
promptEn:
Create an exactly 8-second stylized 3D animation in a fixed, front-facing widescreen composition. Center a single correctly formed Traditional Chinese glyph 犬 in saturated cobalt blue against a softly lit pale apricot background. Use an authentic Traditional Chinese font: one horizontal stroke, a left-falling stroke, a right-falling stroke, and the distinct short dot at the upper right. Preserve the font’s proper intersections and spacing. The complete glyph fills about 70% of frame height, stays centered and uncropped, and remains motionless throughout.

The lead is an original, proudly overconfident wind-up animal band: three small painted wooden cartoon dogs with floppy ears, visible winding keys and expressive hinged jaws. One plays a trumpet, one holds cymbals, and one stands behind a small bass drum. Instruments belong to the band; add no other props. Stage the trio in the generous side margins, with the trumpeter on the left and the other two on the right, leaving every stroke unobstructed. Their curved tails reveal their excitement even while they attempt dignified musician poses.

At 0.0–1.8 seconds, the trumpeter raises its bell, takes an absurdly deep breath with expanding wooden cheeks, and gives the waiting band an earnest nod. At 1.8–2.4, it finally blows: the trumpet produces two soft, unmistakably doglike woofs instead of a musical note. Its ears spring upright and it stares into the bell. The cymbal dog reacts a beat late, accidentally clashing its cymbals at 2.6 seconds; one cymbal gently nudges the adjacent drum. The drum rocks slowly, pauses precariously, then tips flat at 3.3 seconds with a muffled plop. The drummer’s poised mallet taps empty air, and the drummer looks down in a wide-eyed double take. All mishaps are gentle and harmless. At 3.5–4.2 seconds, the trumpeter deliberately gives one tiny successful woof; the others respond with enthusiastic tail wags and a perfectly synchronized bow, proudly accepting their new canine sound. By 4.7 seconds, the trio wheels out through the side edges with all their instruments, the drummer rolling its drum along its rim. Hold only the complete 犬 perfectly still from 4.7–8.0 seconds, providing 3.3 seconds of clear recognition time.

Audio: a warm, friendly off-screen voice speaks clear Taiwanese Mandarin. The entire spoken line is exactly: "犬、犬、警犬". Speak the first 犬 at approximately 0.3–0.8 seconds, the second at 1.1–1.6 seconds, and 警犬 naturally at 5.3–6.3 seconds while the finished glyph is clearly visible. Pronounce 犬 as ㄑㄩㄢˇ and 警犬 as ㄐㄧㄥˇ ㄑㄩㄢˇ, with natural Taiwanese Mandarin tone sandhi. Stop after the word. Keep the brief mechanical ticks, trumpet woofs, cymbal clash and drum plop soft; the dogs have no spoken dialogue. No background music. Use bright, non-neon colors and soft lighting. The single glyph 犬 is the only on-screen text; no vocabulary text, subtitles, logos, watermarks, clutter or flashing effects.
